title: The Mouth That Asks Does Not Get Lost
subtitle: Questions Open the Door to Knowledge and Direction
author: Babi Magil
summary: This proverb teaches that asking questions is a sign of wisdom, not weakness. A person who seeks guidance can find solutions, avoid mistakes, and continue learning throughout life.

sections.heading: The Proverb
content: “The mouth that asks does not get lost.”

sections.heading: Origin & History
content: This proverb comes from African oral wisdom traditions and does not have a confirmed single ethnic owner.
In many African communities, asking elders for guidance has always been an important part of learning. Young people gained knowledge by listening, observing, and respectfully seeking advice.

sections.heading: Meaning
content: The proverb teaches that asking questions helps people discover knowledge and find the right path.
A person who is afraid to ask may remain confused, while someone who seeks advice can learn from the experiences of others.
Questions are not a sign of ignorance; they are a pathway to wisdom.

sections.heading: Cultural Significance
content: Traditional African education was often based on interaction between generations. Children learned through stories, conversations, and guidance from elders.
Respectful questioning was encouraged because it helped preserve knowledge and prevented younger generations from repeating mistakes.

sections.heading: Story
content: Long ago, a young traveler named Dara decided to visit a distant village across the mountains.
He had never traveled that path before, but he was too proud to ask anyone for directions.
An old man at the edge of the village offered to guide him, but Dara replied, 'I can find my way. I do not need help.'
After walking for hours, Dara became lost in the forest.
He finally met a group of farmers and asked, 'Can you please show me the correct path?'
The farmers smiled and guided him safely to his destination.
Dara later returned to the old man and apologized.
The elder told him, 'A question can save you many miles of walking in the wrong direction.'
From that day, Dara understood that asking for knowledge was a sign of intelligence, not weakness.

sections.heading: Life Lessons
content: Never be afraid to ask questions.
Seeking guidance prevents mistakes.
Wisdom grows through communication.
Humility allows people to learn.
The right question can open new opportunities.

sections.heading: Modern Application
content: This proverb applies to education, careers, relationships, and problem-solving. Students, employees, and leaders improve when they ask for clarification and advice.
In a world full of information, knowing how to ask the right questions is a powerful skill.
